newsitem.title: USA: US natgas stocks seen up 80-90 bcf in weekly AGAs.
newsitem.headline: US natgas stocks seen up 80-90 bcf in weekly AGAs.

text.p: U.S. natural gas storage levels were expected to rise by 80 to 90 billion cubic feet (bcf) when weekly American Gas Association (AGA) data are released later today, industry sources said Wednesday.
"The spreads (cash-to-futures) really worked last week and there was a whole lot of mild weather," said one trader, expecting another significant build.

While some expected injections to slow as eastern stocks, now at 80 percent of capacity, fill, others said producing region inventories, lagging at just 60 percent of capacity, could pick up the slack.

"Overall, I don't see injections slowing much next month. The East may slow, but there should be a lot more injections in the South," said another trader, adding favorable cash-to-futures spreads should encourage more stock building.
The Reuter poll of industry players showed expectations for an overall build ranged from 65 bcf to 100 bcf for the week ended September 20. The four-week average is 87 bcf.
Last week, AGA showed overall storage rose by 84 bcf, in line with expectations, but were still 312 bcf, or 12 percent, below the same year-ago period.

Last year at this time, total inventories gained 69 bcf, meaning a build today in the expected range would narrow the gap to last year to about 295 bcf. For the same week in 1995, eastern storage rose by 46 bcf, while producing stocks were up by 19 bcf.
